title: Rabbi Yochanan bar Shaona
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Vayikra Rabbah 5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.5.2), Rabbi Levi reports a teaching in the name of Rabbi Yochanan bar Shaona. Hyman reports that [Bereshit Rabbah 91:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.91.8) reads bar Shaula and that the Arukh, under Bar Hadya, reads bar Shechina. He cites [Seder HaDorot’s proposed identification](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1383&lang=en) with R' Chana Shaona of [Avodah Zarah 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.75a.11).

notes.text: The supplied Tana Shaona form remains a source question; it is not silently changed to a conjectured personal name. Shaona, Shaula and Shechina are preserved as different forms.

The linked Vayikra Rabbah gives Levi’s teaching about the bar hadya bird in the name of Rabbi Yochanan bar Shaona. The linked Bereshit Rabbah gives Sheilah in Levi’s report about Joseph, where Hyman reports Shaula.

[Hyman’s printed notice](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._II._1910.pdf#page=269) gives Bereshit Rabbah 91:8 and Chana, where the supplied transcription has 71:8 and Tana. [The Arukh entry “Bar Hadya”](https://daf-yomi.com/Dictionary.aspx?id=2&tab=browse&wordId=39208) gives Shechina and records Chirya as a variant. The linked Avodah Zarah has Chana Sheina or bar Sheina. Its [parallel in Niddah](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.65b.5) has Chana Shauna or bar Shauna. In both, he transmits from Rabbah bar bar Chana, who transmits from Rabbi Yochanan. Heilprin proposes an identification and questions the claim of direct discipleship.
